This article retains examples based on 24.05; they do not represent the current release or promise compatibility with every model. The nix.dev reference tutorial still targets the Pi 4B. When choosing a nixos-hardware module, pin its revision and read the README for the specific model.
2. Write It to the SD Card

The following dd command overwrites everything on the target device. Back up the SD card first, use lsblk to verify its capacity, model, and mount points, and unmount its partitions. Confirm that /dev/sdX is the entire SD card rather than the system disk. Do not execute the command with the placeholder path unchanged.

The following is a historical Pi 4 configuration skeleton. The root filesystem, boot partition, and kernel are determined by the verified image and hardware module; initially retain the generated hardware-configuration.nix. Listening on all interfaces and opening the firewall expands the reach of the DNS service. Restrict it to the intended LAN interface during deployment and check for port 53 conflicts.

fstrim works only if the storage device and the entire block-device chain support discard; not all SD cards do. tmpfs consumes RAM and potentially swap, so configure it within the memory budget of a low-memory device.
Reducing continuous writes can slow wear. volatile logs are lost on reboot, so external logging is needed to troubleshoot problems across reboots:
First check cooling, power, and load. Adjusting the CPU governor is a performance/power policy; it does not add cooling or guarantee a direct limit on the maximum frequency:

Once the image boots, build your own system configuration first, then schedule nixos-rebuild boot and a reboot. Retain a known-bootable generation and a recovery route through a serial or local console. Unloading network drivers interrupts connectivity; do not do it blindly in a remote session. The placeholder SSH public-key file must actually exist. These configurations have not been tested on a physical Raspberry Pi.
